title: Campaigns
subtitle: Your Google Ads campaign plan, worked out from your store's products, margins and sales.
load_error: We could not load the campaign plan.
no_store_title: Connect your store to get a campaign plan
no_store_desc: The plan starts from your store's catalog, margins and sales.
save_error: We could not save. Please try again.
ready_title: The plan is ready to launch
blocker_ads_account: Choose the Google Ads account to use
blocker_currency: The Google Ads account is in {{account}}, your store in {{store}}: choose an account in {{store}}
blocker_no_offers: No product can enter the campaign right now
existing_ads: Your store already runs Google ads: {{orders}} ({{total}}) in the last 90 days. At launch, Hontrio checks which campaigns run in the account, so the new one does not compete with them for the same products.
goal_hint: Out of the profit on a sale, how much you keep after paying for the ad. With a lower target, Google brings more sales, but each one leaves less profit.
goal_growth_desc: As many sales as possible. You keep ~{{keep}}% of the profit on each.
goal_balanced_desc: Sales and profit in balance. You keep ~{{keep}}% of the profit on each sale.
goal_profit_desc: Fewer sales, but you keep ~{{keep}}% of the profit on each.
goal_roas_unknown: Target ROAS: once you add costs
campaign_hint: What Hontrio will create in your Google Ads account. You pay Google directly for the ads.
type_pmax: Performance Max, from your Merchant Center catalog
type_pmax_hint: One campaign for the whole eligible catalog, feed only: Google builds the ads from your products, shows them on Shopping, Search and the other channels, and learns on its own where they sell. With few sales, one campaign learns faster than several small ones.
bidding_target: Maximize conversion value, with a target ROAS of {{roas}}
bidding_no_target: Maximize conversion value (the target ROAS comes from costs)
bidding_hint: Google bids on every impression so that, on average, each unit spent on ads brings that many back in sales.
budget_hint: To learn, the campaign needs ~{{conversions}} sales a month. At an average order value of {{aov}} and ROAS {{roas}}, that is about {{budget}} a day. Leave empty to use the suggested budget.
budget_hint_no_target: Enter how much you want to spend a day. Once you add costs, Hontrio suggests the right budget.
econ_need_costs: To work out the profit threshold and the target ROAS, add the cost price to the products that sell. Right now {{pct}}% of sales have a cost; at least half is needed.
econ_margin_sales: of the campaign products, from 90 days of sales
econ_margin_catalog: of the campaign products, from cost prices
econ_break_even_sub: below it, the campaign loses money
econ_aov_sub: what Google Ads reports for a sale
adjust_intro: The threshold accounts for what Google Ads receives: the order total.
adjust_vat: Of that, the {{vat}}% VAT does not stay with you.
forecast_title: Per month, if the campaign hits the target
forecast_note: Estimate. Sales include VAT, as Google reports them; profit is without VAT and before fixed costs. The first weeks are for learning, and after launch the real figures appear in Reports.
empty_included: No product enters the campaign right now.
col_break_even_hint: The ROAS from which a sale of the product pays for its ad
no_cost_hint: Add the cost price in Products to see the margin
over_target_hint: Above the {{roas}} target ROAS: at the campaign target, its sales can lose money
footer: The plan is worked out from your synced catalog, website orders from the last 90 days and your cost prices. Removed products stay untouched in Merchant Center: Hontrio only keeps them out of the campaign.
blocker_merchant_woocommerce: Send your products to Merchant Center (Google for WooCommerce)
blocker_conversion_edinio: Set up the purchase conversion in Edinio
blocker_conversion_woocommerce: Measure purchases in Google Ads (Google for WooCommerce)
conversion_ok: Purchase, the one already set up via {{via}} (no new one is created)
conversion_ok_unknown: Purchase, the one already set up (no new one is created)
verified_at_launch: Hontrio cannot ask the plugin from here: we check it at launch, from the Google account.
adjust_vat_assumed: Your store does not calculate VAT, so the math assumes the {{vat}}% standard rate, which you do not keep.
blocker_merchant_shopify: Send your products to Merchant Center (Google & YouTube app)
blocker_conversion_shopify: Measure purchases in Google Ads (Google & YouTube app)
verified_at_launch_shopify: Shopify doesn't tell apps which sales channels a store has (Google & YouTube): we check at launch, from the Google account.
blocker_merchant: Send your products to Merchant Center
action_decided: This proposal has already been decided.
action_not_found: We couldn't find the proposal or campaign.
audit_hint: Before changing anything, Hontrio reads the account: the running campaigns, the purchase conversion, the Merchant Center link and the EU political advertising declaration. The audit changes nothing.
audit_all_ok: The account is ready for launch.
audit_history: Account conversions in the last 30 days: {{conversions}} · active campaigns: {{campaigns}}.
audit_failed: We couldn't check the account. Try again.
audit_no_account: First choose the store's Google Ads account in Settings.
audit_too_soon: You just checked. Wait a minute.
overlap_question: The account already has Shopping or Performance Max campaigns on the same products ({{count}}). What should we do with them?
overlap_pause_hint: recommended: otherwise your campaigns and Hontrio's bid against each other on the same products and push the cost per click up. They aren't deleted; you can resume them anytime.
overlap_keep_hint: the Hontrio campaign gets the lowest Shopping priority so yours come first; with Performance Max, the higher Ad Rank wins anyway.
eu_confirm: I confirm that none of the existing campaigns without a declaration ({{count}}) contains EU political advertising. Google requires the declaration for every campaign; without it, since April 1, 2026, it refuses any change in the account, including the launch.
launch_done: The campaign was created in your Google Ads account and starts within a few hours, after Google's review.
stage_starter_hint: Account conversions in the last 30 days: {{conversions}}, below the 15 Google needs to bid on value by itself. We start with a standard Shopping campaign, with a capped cost per click and a loss limit; once there are enough sales, the autopilot proposes moving to Performance Max.
stage_growth_hint: Account conversions in the last 30 days: {{conversions}}, enough for Google to bid on value by itself. The campaign is a feed-only Performance Max, with the target ROAS starting from what the account achieves now.
type_shopping: Standard Shopping, from the Merchant Center catalog
type_shopping_hint: Product ads only, on Search and the Shopping tab. Every click has a maximum cost and the search terms are visible: we learn cheaply until there are enough sales for Performance Max.
bidding_cpc: Manual CPC, at most {{cpc}} per click
bidding_cpc_hint: What a click may cost so that, at a cautious 1% conversion rate and an average order of {{aov}}, the sale pays for its ad (break-even: ROAS {{roas}}).
bidding_cpc_low: The cap is very low, so the campaign will bring little traffic; with higher margins or larger orders, the cap goes up.
bidding_cpc_unknown: Manual CPC (the cap comes from your costs)
bidding_start_hint: Starts from the ROAS the account achieves now, but not below break-even ({{break_even}}), and moves gradually, at most 12% at a time, toward your goal's target ({{goal}}).
safety_value: The autopilot stops the campaign at {{none}} spent without a single sale, or at {{low}} with ROAS below half of break-even
safety_hint: The loss limit works in approval mode too: it's protection, not optimization. You get a notification and can resume the campaign.
safety_unknown: Calculated once you add your costs
settings_presence: Only people located in the country, not those merely “interested” in it
settings_eu: Declared as containing no EU political advertising (a Google requirement)
settings_utm: Hontrio UTMs on the link, so sales also show up in your store
settings_no_partners: No search partner network, at first
settings_no_expansion: The click always lands on the product page (no URL expansion)
settings_feed_only: Feed only: Google builds the ads from your products
settings_brand: Searches for your store's name stay with your Search campaign: {{terms}}
exclusions_value_one: {{count}} product left out of the campaign
exclusions_value_other: {{count}} products left out of the campaign
exclusions_hint: We leave them out of the campaign only, by their Merchant Center ID. Your feed stays untouched, so they don't disappear from your own campaigns.
exclusions_unmatched_one: {{count}} product to exclude isn't found in Merchant Center yet, so it can't be left out of the campaign; the next sync fixes it.
exclusions_unmatched_other: {{count}} products to exclude aren't found in Merchant Center yet, so they can't be left out of the campaign; the next sync fixes it.
exclusions_label: More than 990 exclusions: Hontrio puts its own label in Merchant Center, in a separate data source, and the campaign uses it.
live_hint: Figures for the last 30 days, pulled daily from Google Ads.
live_footer: Profit is estimated from the store's break-even: the value brought in divided by break-even, minus spend. Google reports sales value including VAT.
pilot_hint: Every day, Hontrio reads the Google Ads figures and sees what's worth changing: the target ROAS, the budget, products that spend without selling, expensive search terms, moving to Performance Max and splitting by margin.
mode_approve_desc: The autopilot proposes, you approve. Nothing changes in the account without you (except stopping at the loss limit).
mode_auto_desc: The autopilot applies changes by itself, within the limits below, and logs them. You get a notification.
max_budget_hint: How far the budget can rise by itself when the campaign is profitable and limited by budget. Without a cap, budget increases stay proposals.
pilot_protective: In either mode, the autopilot changes the target at most once every 14 days (by at most 12%) and the budget at most once a week (by at most 20%), doesn't touch a new Performance Max campaign during its first 6 learning weeks, and stops by itself a campaign that hits the loss limit.
proposals_empty: No proposals right now. The autopilot checks the figures every day.
detail_graduate: Performance Max with target ROAS {{roas}} and a {{budget}}/day budget; the starter campaign stops
detail_segment: High margin: target ROAS {{high}} · the rest: {{rest}}
reason_loss_no_conversions: It hit the loss limit without a single sale. First check that purchases are being measured and that prices are competitive, then resume the campaign.
reason_loss_low_roas: It hit the loss limit with ROAS {{roas}}, below half of break-even ({{break_even}}).
reason_graduate: Account conversions in 30 days: {{conversions}}, enough for Google to bid on value by itself. Performance Max starts with target ROAS {{target}}.
reason_target_below_break_even: The campaign makes ROAS {{actual}}, below break-even ({{break_even}}): the target goes from {{from}} to {{to}} so Google only buys clicks that pay off.
reason_target_toward_goal: The campaign meets its target (ROAS {{actual}}): the target goes from {{from}} to {{to}}, toward your goal.
reason_target_too_strict: The target of {{from}} holds the campaign back (it spends under 70% of the budget, at ROAS {{actual}}): we lower it to {{to}}, but not below break-even.
reason_budget_limited: The campaign is limited by budget and makes ROAS {{actual}}, above target: more budget brings more profitable sales.
reason_exclude_products_one: One product spent over the last 30 days without bringing profit: we leave it out of campaigns (you can include it again from the plan).
reason_exclude_products_other: {{count}} products spent over the last 30 days without bringing profit: we leave them out of campaigns (you can include them again from the plan).
reason_negatives_one: One search term spent without any sale: we add it as an exact negative.
reason_negatives_other: {{count}} search terms spent without any sale: we add them as exact negatives.
reason_segment: Products have different break-evens (ROAS {{high_be}} for high margin, {{rest_be}} for the rest): two campaigns, each with its own target, spend better than one.
reason_sync_products_one: The plan changed: the campaign now excludes one product.
reason_sync_products_other: The plan changed: the campaign now excludes {{count}} products.
blocker_audit: Check the Google Ads account (the audit below)
blocker_account_manager: The chosen account is a manager account: choose the store's advertiser account
blocker_merchant_not_linked: Link Merchant Center to the Google Ads account
blocker_merchant_other: The store's Merchant Center ({{merchant}}) isn't linked to this Google Ads account
blocker_merchant_choose: The account has several linked Merchant Centers ({{count}}): choose the store's one in Settings
blocker_purchase_missing: Create the purchase conversion in Google Ads
blocker_purchase_not_primary: Make the purchase conversion primary so Google bids on it
blocker_purchase_no_value: Send the order value with the purchase conversion
blocker_too_many_exclusions: Too many products to exclude ({{count}}) for the campaign's list: choose the Merchant Center account so Hontrio can add its label
check_account_manager: The chosen account is a manager account: campaigns only run in advertiser accounts.
check_currency_mismatch: The account currency ({{account}}) differs from the store's ({{store}}).
check_auto_tagging_off: Auto-tagging (gclid) is off: Google can't connect clicks to orders. Turn it on in the Google Ads account settings.
check_merchant_not_linked: No Merchant Center is linked to this Google Ads account. Link it from Google Ads (Tools → Linked accounts) or from Merchant Center.
check_merchant_other: The store's Merchant Center ({{merchant}}) isn't linked to this account, and Shopping campaigns need the link.
check_merchant_choose: The account has {{count}} linked Merchant Center accounts: choose the store's one in Settings.
check_purchase_missing: There's no active purchase conversion. Without it, Google doesn't know which clicks become sales.
check_purchase_not_primary: The purchase conversion exists but isn't “primary”: Google doesn't use it for bidding.
check_purchase_no_value: The purchase conversion always uses the same value, not the order value: value-based bidding can't work.
check_no_recent_conversions: No conversions in the last 30 days: check that the tag fires on the order confirmation page.
check_eu_undeclared: Campaigns without the EU political advertising declaration: {{count}}. Google refuses any change in the account until they're declared; you can declare them at launch.
check_overlap: Shopping or Performance Max campaigns on the same products: {{count}}. Choose below what we do with them.
check_search_active: The account has a Search campaign: searches for your store's name stay with it (a negative keyword in the Hontrio campaign).
